# Setting up easy simulations

```{r}
easy_sim <- function(nobs, beta1, beta2){
  sim <- simulateTwoCauseFineGrayModel(nobs = 50,
                                          beta1 = beta1,
                                          beta2 = beta2,
                                          X = NULL,
                                          u.min = 100,
                                          u.max = 100,
                                          p = 0.5,
                                          returnX = TRUE)
  
  sim_data <- cbind(data.frame(ID = nobs,
                            TTE = sim$ftime,
                            Status = as.integer(sim$fstatus)),
                       sim$X)
  
  names(sim_data)<- c("ID", "TTE", "Status", paste0("X_", 4:ncol(sim_data)))
  
  x <- as.matrix(sim_data %>%select(starts_with("X")))
  y <- as.matrix(sim_data %>%
  mutate(Status = as.numeric(Status))%>%
  select(TTE, Status))
  
  return(list("dataframe" = sim_data,
              "x" = x,
              "y" = y))
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(3149)
p5 <- easy_sim(50,
               c(0.40, - 0.50, 0.60, 0.75, - 0.80),
               c(0, 0.3, 0, 0, -0.2)
               )

p10 <- easy_sim(50,
               c(0.40, - 0.50, 0.60, 0.75, - 0.80, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
               c(0, 0.3, 0, 0, -0.2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
               )
```

```{r}

```

```{r}
ggplot(test, aes(x = s1, y = score_mean, color = as.factor(s0))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  # Add error bars to show the +/- 1 standard deviation
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = score_mean - score_sd, 
                    ymax = score_mean + score_sd), 
                width = 0.02, alpha = 0.6) +
  # Faceting by s0 makes it much easier to read than a spaghetti plot
  facet_wrap(~ s0, labeller = label_both) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Score Trends and Fold Volatility",
    subtitle = "Shorter error bars indicate a more stable, reliable model",
    x = "Parameter s1",
    y = "Score Mean (+/- 1 SD)",
    color = "s0"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") # Facets already tell us the s0 value
```

```{r}
library(ggrepel) # Optional: helps prevent text labels from overlapping

ggplot(test, aes(x = score_sd, y = score_mean, color = as.factor(s0))) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Optional: label the top 5 models so you know which settings they are
  geom_text_repel(
    data = subset(test, score_mean > quantile(score_mean, 0.90)), # labels top 10%
    aes(label = paste("s0:", s0, "\ns1:", s1)),
    size = 3
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Performance vs. Stability Trade-off",
    subtitle = "Ideal models are in the top-left (High Mean, Low Variance)",
    x = "Score Standard Deviation (Lower is better)",
    y = "Mean Score (Higher is better)",
    color = "s0"
  )
```

# BB-SSL

```{r}
#source("~/Documents/bhCRR/analyses/scratch/bb_ssl.r")
```

```{r}
bb_ssl <- function(x, y,
                   NSample,
                   ss = c(0.04, 0.5),
                   lambda = 1 / ss,
                   alpha = 3,
                   theta = 0.5,
                   jitter = TRUE,
                   discard = FALSE,
                   progress = TRUE,
                   ...) {

  x <- as.matrix(x)
  y <- as.matrix(y)
  n <- nrow(x)
  p <- ncol(x)

  lambda0 <- lambda[1]   # spike rate (large)
  lambda1 <- lambda[2]   # slab  rate (small)
  if (lambda0 <= lambda1) {
    warning("Expected lambda0 (spike) >> lambda1 (slab); got lambda = c(",
            lambda0, ", ", lambda1, ").")
  }

  # Mean-zero Laplace sampler with scale b  (difference of two Exp(rate = 1/b))
  rlaplace0 <- function(m, b) {
    stats::rexp(m, rate = 1 / b) - stats::rexp(m, rate = 1 / b)
  }

  beta  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = NSample, ncol = p)
  gamma <- matrix(0L,       nrow = NSample, ncol = p)
  pips <- matrix(0L,       nrow = NSample, ncol = p)

  pb <- if (progress) utils::txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = NSample, style = 3)

  i <- 1L
  while (i <= NSample) {

    # (a) sample weights  w ~ n * Dirichlet(alpha, ..., alpha)
    w <- stats::rgamma(n, shape = alpha, rate = 1)
    w <- w * (n / sum(w))

    # (b) sample jitter   mu_j ~ Laplace(0, scale = 1/lambda0)  [the spike]
    mu <- if (jitter) rlaplace0(p, b = 1 / lambda0) else rep(0, p)

    # (c) optimise tilde-beta_t.
    #     Bayesian-bootstrap resample of rows with probabilities w / n,
    #     then refit fit_ssl_psdh (replacing SSLASSO_2) on the resample.
    idx     <- sample.int(n, size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = w / n)
    fit     <- fit_ssl_psdh(x[idx, , drop = FALSE],
                            y[idx, , drop = FALSE],
                            ss = ss, ...)

    if (isTRUE(discard) && isFALSE(fit$conv)) next  # redraw if EM didn't converge

    beta_hat <- fit$coefficients[,2]
    beta[i, ] <- beta_hat + mu                      # post-hoc location shift
    pips[i,] <- fit$pips


    # threshold beta -> gamma  (posterior inclusion under the SSL prior)
    #   p* = 1 / (1 + (1-theta)/theta * (lambda0/lambda1) * exp(-(lambda0-lambda1)|beta|))
    odds <- (1 - theta) / theta *
            (lambda0 / lambda1) * exp(-(lambda0 - lambda1) * abs(beta[i, ]))
    pstar <- 1 / (1 + odds)
    pstar[is.na(pstar)] <- 1
    gamma[i, ] <- as.integer(pstar > 0.5)

    if (progress) {
      utils::setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)
      if (i == NSample) close(pb)
    }
    i <- i + 1L
  }

  colnames(beta) <- colnames(gamma) <-
    if (is.null(colnames(x))) paste0("V", seq_len(p)) else colnames(x)

  list(beta           = beta,
       gamma          = gamma,
       pips = pips,
       inclusion_prob = colMeans(pips),
       post_mean      = colMeans(beta),
       ss             = ss,
       lambda         = c(lambda0 = lambda0, lambda1 = lambda1),
       alpha          = alpha)
}

```

```{r}
post2 <- bb_ssl(
  p10$x, p10$y,
  NSample = 50,
  ss      = c(0.005, 0.5),   # scales -> fit_ssl_psdh
  alpha   = 3,
  initial_sparsity = 0.5,  # ... forwarded to fit_ssl_psdh
  maxit   = 50,
  fixed_global_shrinkage = NULL
)
```
